title: Pullback of internal Hom from a finite projective constant module
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $g:S'\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves $A_S$ and $A_{S'}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. For a finite projective $A$-module $M$ (a direct summand of a finite free $A$-module), write $\underline M_S$ for its constant $A_S$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every $A_S$-module sheaf $F$, the canonical map [def-pur-sheaf-hom]
$$g^*\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(\underline M_S,F)\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_{A_{S'}}(g^*\underline M_S,g^*F)$$
obtained by pulling back the evaluation pairing and currying with the tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] and the sheaf tensor-Hom adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] (using [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]) is an isomorphism. It is natural in $M$ and $F$, and under this map the pulled-back evaluation pairing is the evaluation pairing for $g^*\underline M_S$ and $g^*F$.

source.place: Tag 0GM7, label lemma-pullback-internal-hom, proof of (1): the strictly perfect calculation and the final finite-projective identity $h^*\mathcal Hom(\mathcal E,\mathcal F)=\mathcal Hom(h^*\mathcal E,h^*\mathcal F)$

proof.text: Because $M$ is finite projective, choose an integer $r\ge0$ and $A$-linear maps $i:M\to A^{\oplus r}$ and $p:A^{\oplus r}\to M$ with $p\circ i=1_M$. Applying the constant-sheaf construction gives a split pair $\underline M_S\xrightarrow{\underline i}\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_S\xrightarrow{\underline p}\underline M_S$. The exact inverse-image theorem identifies $g^*\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_S$ with $\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_{S'}$ and carries this splitting to the corresponding one for $g^*\underline M_S$, because it preserves compositions and identities.

source.place: Tag 0GM7, proof of (1), locality paragraph and final finite-projective direct-summand sentence

proof.text: For the free module $A^{\oplus r}$, the sheaf tensor--Hom adjunction and the standard basis identify $\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_S,F)$ with $F^{\oplus r}$: a map is determined by its values on the $r$ basis vectors, and the inverse sends $(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$ to the map $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_jf_j$. The same description on $S'$ identifies $\mathcal Hom_{A_{S'}}(g^*\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_S,g^*F)$ with $(g^*F)^{\oplus r}$. Additivity and exactness of $g^*$, its identification of the constant ring sheaf, and the canonical tensor comparison identify the pullback of the first $r$-fold sum with the second; in these coordinates the canonical comparison is the identity. The coordinate evaluation map is therefore carried to the coordinate evaluation map.

source.place: Tag 0GM7, proof of (1), final calculation for a direct summand of a finite free module

proof.text:
Let $c_E:g^*\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(\underline E_S,F)\to\mathcal Hom_{A_{S'}}(g^*\underline E_S,g^*F)$ denote the comparison for $E$. Its construction by pulling back evaluation and currying makes it natural in $E$ and $F$. For the splitting in Step 1, the inverse to $c_M$ is the explicit composite
$$\mathcal Hom_{A_{S'}}(g^*\underline M_S,g^*F)\xrightarrow{\,\mathcal Hom(g^*\underline p,g^*F)\,}\mathcal Hom_{A_{S'}}(g^*\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_S,g^*F)\xrightarrow{\,c_{A^{\oplus r}}^{-1}\,}g^*\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(\underline{A^{\oplus r}}_S,F)\xrightarrow{\,g^*\mathcal Hom(\underline i,F)\,}g^*\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(\underline M_S,F).$$
Naturality gives the two inverse identities, since both reduce to $p i=1_M$; hence $c_M$ is an isomorphism. The same naturality calculation carries the pulled-back evaluation to evaluation after pullback, and proves naturality in both $M$ and $F$.

The statement is true. It is the degree-zero finite-projective term identity of 0GM7(1), specialised to small etale sites with constant A coefficients. The base change is the exact constant inverse image of prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact, which by its clause (2) is the u^* of the tensor-comparison node; the coefficient category Mod(A_T) is unchanged. The worker correctly reports and fixes the Stacks typo Hom(h^*E,F). Checked cases: M=0, M=A, M=A^r, M=Ae for an idempotent e (Z/6), g=id, S' empty, F=0. Step 1: the split pair survives the constant sheaf and g^* by functoriality, prop (1) and additivity (3). Step 2: c_A is an iso because the transpose of phi is phi composed with the inverse right unitor, where phi is the unit iso, the tensor comparison and g^* of the unitor; this does not even need the 'identity in coordinates' claim. Step 3: I verified both inverse identities of the retract formula by hand. proof_deps equals the union of uses, there is no cycle, and all cited units lie on the route (no tool_uses needed or accepted).
